    StartersPip's acorn nutsHoney and cinnamon nuts. Pip can't say a word in New York.How to make it150g hazelnuts150g almonds3 tbsp honey1/2 tsp ground cinnamonToss the hazelnuts and almonds with the honey and cinnamon.Spread on a lined tray.Roast at 170°C, stirring once.Cool on baking paper, then break into clusters.Central Park pretzels with cheddar dipThe Central Park song, That's How You KnowHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chewy soft pretzels dipped in a bicarb bath, salted and baked deep brown, with a warm sharp cheddar and mustard dip.Divide 500g pizza dough into 8, roll into long ropes and twist into pretzels.Boil 2L water with 4 tbsp bicarb soda and dip each for 30 seconds.Brush with egg, sprinkle with sea salt and bake at 220°C for 12 minutes.For the dip, melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp plain flour, whisk in 250ml milk until thick, then stir in 150g grated cheddar and 1 tsp mustard until smooth.MainsPancakes, bacon and scrambled eggsButtermilk pancakes with crisp bacon and soft scrambled eggsHow to make it250g plain flour2 tsp baking powder6 eggs375ml buttermilk40g butter, for cooking8 rashers of bacon250g strawberries100ml maple syrupWhisk the flour, baking powder, 2 of the eggs and the buttermilk into a batter.Cook the pancakes in half the butter in the pan and keep warm.Fry the bacon until crisp.Scramble the remaining eggs softly in the rest of the butter.Slice the strawberries.Pile everything onto big plates with the maple syrup on the side.King and Queen's ball eye filletThe ball where Robert dances. He never said he couldn't.How to make itAs written, serves 4Beef eye fillet roasted pink with a creamy mushroom and thyme sauce, potato gratin and grilled asparagus, dinner fit for a fairytale ball.Layer 1kg thinly sliced potatoes with 300ml cream, garlic and salt and bake at 180°C for 1 hour.Sear a seasoned 1kg eye fillet and roast at 200°C for 20 minutes, then rest 10 minutes.In the same pan, fry 250g sliced mushrooms in 30g butter, add thyme, 200ml beef stock and 150ml cream, and simmer until thick.Grill 2 bunches asparagus.Slice the beef and spoon over the sauce.SweetsPoison apple toffee applesToffee apples. Poison ones don't grow on trees, says Narissa.How to make it6 red apples6 wooden sticks400g caster sugar150ml waterred food colouring, a few dropsPush a stick into each apple.Boil the sugar, water and red colouring to 150°C without stirring.Dip each apple and twist to coat.Set on baking paper and leave to harden.Pink meringues and dipped strawberriesPink meringue kisses and strawberries dipped in white chocolateHow to make it2 egg whites120g caster sugarpink food colouring, a drop250g strawberries200g white chocolateedible glitter, to dustWhisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, adding the sugar a spoon at a time and a drop of pink colouring.Pipe small kisses onto lined trays.Bake at 100°C until crisp, then cool on the tray.Cool the meringues completely.Melt the white chocolate gently.Dip the strawberries halfway in the chocolate and set on baking paper.Dust with edible glitter and serve both together.DrinksGiselle's pink lemonade floatRaspberry lemonade with soda water and a scoop of lemon sorbetHow to make it250g raspberries100g caster sugar4 lemons800ml chilled soda water500ml lemon sorbet4 mint leavesBlend half the raspberries with the sugar and lemon juice, then strain through a sieve.Stir the strained mix into the soda water in a jug.Put a scoop of sorbet into each tall glass.Slowly pour over the pink lemonade so it foams up.Drop in a few whole raspberries and a mint leaf, and serve with a spoon and a straw.
